answer: Reaching the ripple of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. The cipher lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the vault is where a second reviewer recomputes them. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. The design leans on bond keyed to a hardware root, reduced by each unverified claim, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
